item.title: First article?
item.content:encoded: Why not start by hinting that the highest level of the foundation isn’t actually the highest with the most basic no detail story ever. Yea that sounds like a first try kind of plot to me! Try a 173 type article before you do a 001.

Need to read it again and see if I'm missing something more than that, though.

I really want to keep these last couple paragraphs vague if I can get away with it!

I agree, I just meant you could clear it up a bit without being too obvious. For instance:

An hour after MTF units gained access to his apartment, PoI-5297 entered the building. The MTF units moved to apprehend him. After a brief conversation, the MTF released PoI-5297, who sent a text message to an unknown person and left the building.

This way the chronology is more clear without explaining what exactly he told them.

item.content:encoded:
aw! thanks—and thanks for all the feedback, too!

(and for adding those tags, because i had absolutely no idea how to do that)

i've made most of the edits you've suggested—with a couple exceptions:

+ show block
– hide block

"generally note you don't store anomalies at green sites"

I did not know this! That said, I think it makes sense for 5297 to be an exception; given how manifestly paranoid and secretive the O5 are about its contents, it seems like they'd want it kept as close as possible, normal protocol be damned.

"I would consider saying 'whose documentation is classified at Level-4 or higher.'"

I ended up keeping the original wording here—I think saying something is classified "Level-4 or higher" might end up leading a reader to mistakenly think I'm just saying "classified Level-4" but with extra words.

"I think this could be cleared up a bit without being too explicit. As far as I can tell, what happened here is that PoI-5297 told something compromising to the task force to get them to release him."

I really want to keep these last couple paragraphs vague if I can get away with it! Blackmail is definitely a possibility I'm implying, but it's not the only possibility I'm implying, if you catch my drift. (TERRIBLE_WIKIDOT_WINK_EMOTICON.JPEG)

Anyway—thanks again!

thanks! i'm glad you liked it!

as far as the details in the article go, i had it in my head that this whole report became "O5 eyes only" pretty much as soon as they realized what was in 5297, because otherwise you're right—they wouldn't want the rest of the Foundation to be privy to any of this. i should make that clear in the piece itself, though—see if i can't track down a "LEVEL-5 CLASSIFIED" banner someplace.

i'm gonna have to think about what to do re: that picture! think it's a lot more inviting and visually appealing than a photo of some papers would be, but you're right—it's not actually super-relevant to the actual article. i don't want to go image-less—maybe there's a fourth option i'm not seeing?

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
For a first time work, this is pretty great. I like the confusion with something that just feels so anomalous, but evidently isn't. You can see the human element of the Foundation, as people's information is scrutinized or revealed and people feel vulnerable over the very existence of this document. The implicit suggestion of blackmail was also great.

Or I'm just a sucker for -EX scips. Either way, +1.

That said, there are a lot of small weaknesses that bring this article short of greatness.

+ Show nitpicks
- Hide nitpicks

Explained/Neutralized

Object classifications are for determining difficulty of containment, if an object is not considered to be anomalous, whether it's "neutralized" or extant is not relevant. "Neutralization" implies it was once anomalous, here, it never was.

The Judiciary Square neighborhood of Washington, D.C. SCP-5297-EX was recovered several hundred meters from the location of this photograph.

Given you explain the discovery later, I would just make this "Judiciary Square in Washington, D.C.".

Site 01

Site-01. Though generally note you don't store anomalies at green sites, though I'm willing to let this pass since it's not clear when they discovered it wasn't anomalous.

POI-5297-1

It's usually PoI. Also not sure why it's -1, given there isn't a PoI -2. Imo it should just be PoI-5297, but that doesn't matter too much.

Update—1/15/2019

You should use the international date standard to avoid confusion between American and European-style dates.

including several whose documentation is classified Level 4 or Level 5.

Level-4 or Level-5. Also I would consider saying "whose documentation is classified at Level-4 or higher."

prominent SCP Foundation officials.

I found it kind of weird that you call it the "Foundation" but switch to "SCP Foundation" for this one line, to no apparent effect.

The MTF units moved to apprehend him. After a brief conversation, POI-5297-1 sent a text message to an unknown person and left the building.

I think this could be cleared up a bit without being too explicit. As far as I can tell, what happened here is that PoI-5297 told something compromising to the task force to get them to release him.

I like this one, it's weird and interesting and had me genuinely curious throughout. It gets a little goofy with the description of the O5 council and their behavior, but that's not a total dealbreaker. My bigger concern is why the O5 council would allow such details to be printed in the SCP report in the first place, since there's clearly a secret here that they're trying to cover up. In that same vein, I think the name of the intern should probably be black box'd or redacted.

The picture seems pretty random - "here's a location sort of near where it was found" isn't particularly interesting. I'd suggest finding or making an image of the document itself instead, if you feel like you need to have an image.

item.content:encoded:
hello! long-time reader, first-time skipper!

i wanted to make something gripping in honor of July 4, the most terrifying time of year—so I wrote up an article about the scariest thing I could think of: a city government's intern forgetting his backpack.

(The source for the page's lone image is https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Judiciary_Square_station_entrance_pylon.jpg, which is in the public domain.)

thanks for your time!

EDIT: also! big ups to IHP and QuantumSpace for checking out my draft (and being patient with me while I flailed confusedly around IRC for the first time)!

EDIT EDIT: the article's image has been changed; the new image's source is https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Lever_arch_file.jpg, taken by Pavel Kronk and covered by the Creative Commons Attribution-Share Alike 2.5 Generic license. (I've also made a few minor edits and added a classified banner; thanks to aismallard for pointing me to the SCP style resource and making some formatting edits!)
